content: 1. For uncomplicated infections, administer 1 gram of cefotaxime intravenously (IV) or intramuscularly (IM) every 12 hours. 2. For moderate to severe infections, administer 1 to 2 grams of cefotaxime IV or IM every 8 hours. 3. For more serious infections, such as bloodstream infections (septicemia), administer 2 grams of cefotaxime IV every 6 to 8 hours. 4. For life-threatening infections, administer 2 grams of cefotaxime IV every 4 hours, not exceeding a total daily dose of 12 grams. 5. For surgical infection prophylaxis, administer 1 gram of cefotaxime IV or IM once, 30 to 90 minutes before the start of the procedure. 6. For pediatric patients under 12 years of age or weighing less than 50 kg, administer 50 to 200 mg/kg/day of cefotaxime IV or IM, divided every 6 to 8 hours. 7. For patients over 12 years of age or weighing more than 50 kg, administer 1 to 2 grams of cefotaxime IV or IM every 8 hours. 8. For pediatric patients under 12 years of age or weighing less than 50 kg with severe infections, administer 150 to 200 mg/kg/day of cefotaxime IV or IM, divided every 6 hours, in combination with clindamycin for 7 to 10 days. 9. For patients over 12 years of age or weighing more than 50 kg with severe infections, administer 2 grams of cefotaxime IV every 4 to 6 hours, in combination with other antimicrobial therapy as necessary. 10. For fluoroquinolone-resistant infections, administer 80 mg/kg/day of cefotaxime IV or IM, divided every 6 to 8 hours, not exceeding 12 grams per day. 11. Cefotaxime decreases the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines, such as the BCG vaccine, due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is complete. 12. Avoid coadministration of the cholera vaccine with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may be active against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 13. Cefotaxime may reduce the efficacy of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores. Complete antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 14. Cefotaxime increases the nephrotoxic and/or ototoxic effects of aminoglycosides, such as amikacin, gentamicin, kanamycin, neomycin, streptomycin, and tobramycin. Use caution and monitor renal and auditory function closely. 15. Cefotaxime may increase the toxicity of voclosporin by nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 16. Cefotaxime increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor coagulation parameters. 17. Probenecid increases the levels or effects of cefotaxime by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Cefotaxime decreases the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors, such as atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, camrelizumab, cemiplimab, dostarlimab, durvalumab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, penpulimab, retifanlimab, sintilimab, tislelizumab, and toripalimab, through unspecified interaction mechanisms. Use caution and monitor closely, as coadministration may interfere with therapeutic effects. 19. Cefotaxime decreases the levels or effects of oral contraceptives, such as ethinylestradiol, dienogest/estradiol valerate, and levonorgestrel/ethinylestradiol/ferrous bisglycinate, by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of hormones. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but additional or alternative forms of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 20. Cefotaxime decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Cefotaxime increases the levels or effects of acidic (anionic) drugs, such as aminohippurate sodium, choline magnesium trisalicylate, sulfasalazine, and willow bark, by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 22. Chloramphenicol decreases the effects of cefotaxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Cefotaxime increases the toxicity of plazomicin by nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Cefotaxime decreases the effects of live typhoid vaccines through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Live bacterial vaccines should not be administered until antibiotic therapy is complete. 25. Rose hips may increase the levels or effects of cefotaxime by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown.
